reason: The text contains several named individual characters who are regular people. Most prominently, גִּדְעוֹן (Gideon) is a named character explicitly described as a regular person - he is a farmer and explicitly identifies himself as 'the youngest in my father's house' (הַצָּעִיר בְּבֵית אָבִי), indicating humble ordinary status. יוֹאָשׁ (Joash), Gideon's father, is also a named character who is clearly a regular person. Additionally, עֹרֵב (Oreb) and זְאֵב (Zeeb) are named Midianite leaders/princes who are regular (non-divine) persons. The text is populated with named human characters despite also containing references to God and divine messengers.
